security.rationale: Owner-rights is deliberate so anon can read only the structural public projection while holding zero base-table SELECT. The view has a fixed 21-column allowlist, an internal Approved+active+public_visibility+credit row predicate, and all write privileges are revoked and asserted by migration.

These helpers are referenced by authenticated RLS policies. PUBLIC and anon EXECUTE are revoked; authenticated/service_role EXECUTE is intentional. Each returns only a current-user authorization boolean and does not expose row data or mutate business state.

The project is on Pro and the control should be enabled before broad password-auth growth. It does not affect scale architecture or authority correctness. Phase 26 owns the production Auth hardening bundle so password-strength, leaked-password, reauthentication and MFA controls are changed and regression-tested together rather than piecemeal.
These tables are RLS-on with no browser policy, which denies anon/authenticated Data API access while service-role/server authorities remain explicit.

performance.rationale: Do not add indexes blindly. Phase 8 already certified bounded matching plans; add FK indexes when representative query/delete/update plans justify them.
Current usage statistics are not sufficient evidence to remove future-path or low-frequency safety indexes.
Policies are functionally correct; this is a performance lint. Phase 20 preserves authorization semantics and records it for measured RLS optimization.
Current Auth max 10 connection allocation is adequate at present; switch to percentage allocation when compute is resized.
